newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thais toughen penalty for amphetamine trafficking.
newsitem.headline: Thais toughen penalty for amphetamine trafficking.

text.p: A new Thai law that increases the maximum penalty for amphetamine traffickers to the death penalty will take effect on Wednesday, an official at the Office of Narcotics Control Board (ONCB) said.

In an effort to stem rising amphetamine use in Thailand, the public health minister issued a decree that removes the drugs from the legal medicine list and reclassifies them as first rate narcotics, the official said.
Anyone found guilty of possessing more than 20 grams (0.7 ounces) of amphetamines will be considered a trafficker, and the maximum penalty for trafficking narcotics is death.
The sentence used to be a 100,000 baht ($4,000) fine and five to 20 years in prison, the official said.
Amphetamines stimulate the central nervous system and can make a user violent, the ONCB said in a statement.
The number of cases of people on amphetamines who have committed violent crimes, taken hostages or threatened suicide had been on the rise in Thailand, the statement said.
In the first six months of 1996 police seized more than one tonne of amphetamines, the ONCB said. This compares to seizures totalling 500 kg for all of 1995.
Statistics compiled by the Thailand Development Research Institute show that as of December 1994 about 1.3 million people in Thailand were drug addicts -- 80 percent of them addicted to amphetamines.
But member of parliament Sophon Phetsawang recently said the lastest data shows at least four million of Thailand's 60 million citizens are addicted to amphetamines.
"The amphetamines have penetrated into every walk of life, including schoolchildren and Buddhist monks," Sophon told parliament last month. ($1.00=25 baht)
